title: 2008 AMC 12A Problem 17
statement: Let \(a_1,\) \(a_2,\) \(\ldots\) be a sequence of integers determined by the rule \(a_n = \frac{a_{n-1}}{2}\) if \(a_{n-1}\) is even and \(a_n = 3a_{n-1} + 1\) if \(a_{n-1}\) is odd. For how many positive integers \(a_1 \le 2008\) is it true that \(a_1\) is less than each of \(a_2,\) \(a_3,\) and \(a_4?\)

solutions.text:
If \(a_1\) is even, then \(a_2 = \frac{a_1}{2} \lt a_1,\) so the condition fails.

If \(a_1 \equiv 1 \pmod 4,\) then \(a_2 = 3a_1 + 1\) is a multiple of \(4,\) so \(a_3 = \frac{3a_1 + 1}{2}\) and \(a_4 = \frac{3a_1 + 1}{4} \le a_1,\) and again the condition fails.

If \(a_1 \equiv 3 \pmod 4,\) then \(a_2\) is even but not a multiple of \(4,\) so \(a_3 = \frac{3a_1 + 1}{2} \gt a_1,\) and \(a_3\) is odd, giving \(a_4 = 3a_3 + 1 \gt a_3 \gt a_1.\) The condition holds.

Exactly \(\tfrac{2008}{4} = 502\) values of \(a_1 \le 2008\) satisfy \(a_1 \equiv 3 \pmod 4.\)

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: If \(a_1\) is even then \(a_2 \lt a_1,\) so \(a_1\) must be odd
Split the odd case according to whether \(a_1 \equiv 1\) or \(a_1 \equiv 3 \pmod 4\)
